analysis.investment_thesis: Rikhav Securities is a stockbroker — a financial company that my Magic Formula explicitly excludes because working-capital and debt conventions distort ROIC and EBIT/EV. Even ignoring that rule, EBIT collapsed from INR 55 Cr (2024) to INR 34 Cr (2025) and ROCE of 16.7% sits below my 20%+ threshold.
key_strengths: Earnings yield ~21% (EBIT 34 / EV ~164 Cr) screens cheap on headline basis
Revenue CAGR 108.9% over 3Y with net debt near zero (borrowings just 5 Cr vs equity 244 Cr)
Promoter holding 64% — aligned skin in the game
key_risks: Financial/brokerage business — cyclical commission income tied to retail market euphoria
Operating profit fell 38% YoY (55→34 Cr) and OCF swung to -188 Cr in 2025
ROCE 16.7% and ROE 12.9% are mediocre; only 1 of last 4 years had positive OCF
red_flags: Financial services company — excluded from Magic Formula by rule
EBIT and net profit both declined in FY25 despite revenue 3x'ing (margin compression from 50% to 10%)
Highly negative and volatile operating cash flow inconsistent with reported earnings
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula ranks companies on earnings yield (EBIT/EV) and return on capital, but I deliberately exclude financials and utilities because their balance sheets — where "inventory" is client float and leverage is structural — make these ratios meaningless. Rikhav is a pure-play broker, so the 21% earnings yield screen is misleading: much of the reported revenue jump to INR 328 Cr and the swings in OCF (-37, -9, +109, -188) reflect client settlement flows, not durable owner earnings.

Even setting the exclusion aside, the fundamentals don't pass the "good business" test. ROCE of 16.7% is below my 20% bar, operating income dropped from INR 55 Cr to INR 34 Cr year-on-year, and margins compressed from ~50% to ~10% as revenue scaled — a classic sign of low-quality top-line growth. The P/E of 6.6x looks cheap, but it's cheap for a reason: broker earnings mean-revert hard when market cycles turn. Pass.
